$comment: Per-repo settings read by the sydevs `workflow` plugin. This repo is unusual: it holds the plugin itself, so a change here changes how every other repo is worked on. It has no package manager and no build.
packageManagerNote: There is no package.json. The hooks are plain node .mjs files run by Claude Code directly; nothing is installed or bundled.

leanGate.contents: Plugin manifest + skill frontmatter validation. There is no test suite — the skills are prose, and their real gate is a supervised loop run.

securityReview.rationale: Hooks execute in a maintainer's session with their credentials, and a SKILL.md is an instruction to an agent holding write access to five repos. A prompt-injection or an over-broad allowed-tools line is this repo's equivalent of an RCE. loop-config.json carries the ceilings and the identity constant.

deployTarget: Consumed live from `main` by the Claude routines and by `/plugin install workflow@sydevs`. There is no release step: merging to main IS the deploy, and the next routine run picks it up.
prAllowlistNote: THE WHOLE REPO is ticketless: any change here may go straight to a PR with no `ready-to-implement` issue. The ticket gate exists so the loop does not write code nobody asked for, and it buys nothing here — this repo ships prose and config, the PR body IS the proposal, and a ticket restating it only adds a round trip before the same reviewer reads the same argument. What still gates the work is unchanged and is the part that matters: merging needs an approving review, `wipCapPerRepo` bounds how many PRs may be open at once, and the loop must never merge here (`mergePolicy.loopMayNotMerge` in loop-config.json), so a human reading the PR is the only gate its changes pass. A ticket remains the right shape when the change needs a DECISION before code — competing designs, or anything whose cost is worth agreeing before it is paid.
selfModificationNote: The loop edits its own instructions here. Two consequences worth stating: a bad merge to main degrades every subsequent run with no rollback other than another PR, and the loop cannot validate a skill change by running it — the change only takes effect on the NEXT run. Prefer small, reversible edits, and never ship a skill change and a ceiling change in the same PR.
journalNote: Journal issues live in this repo carrying the `ops-journal` label. They are the loop's own diary, never work. Every worklist query must exclude that label — `-label:ops-journal` — or the loop will pick up its own entries as tickets.
